text:
Jordan (Support): Hey team, escalated from customer ACME. They report lots of 429s and "perceived throttling" when they send bursts after idle periods. They use continuous batching + KV cache. Customer says things look fine during steady traffic but after a quiet window, a burst of ~200 small requests (chat completions) results in ~40% 429s. They sent logs, repro steps below. Case: #ACME-4982.

Priya (SRE): Thanks Jordan. Can you paste the raw 429 snippet and which model/route they're hitting? Also any X-RateLimit headers in the response?

Jordan (Support): Paste from their app logs (sanitized):

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 14:23:02 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: r-1a2b3c
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1675934602
{
  "error": "Rate limit exceeded",
  "code": "rate_limit_exceeded"
}
```

They hit our /v1/chat/completions with model=redwood-medium, token use very low per request (~60 tokens). They also show this header variant for some requests: `X-Quota-Remaining: -12` which is odd.

Eli (Billing): Negative remaining is usually a sign quota accounting bumped incorrectly — maybe double-counting tokens or a stale cache. Jordan, do we know whether these requests are hitting dedicated capacity or hosted? Customer is on Hosted (metered).

Jordan (Support): Hosted. They also use KV prefix-caching on the prompt side — they prepopulate KV so most requests should hit the cache. Customer suspects the KV cold-start + continuous batching interaction is making the server overcount tokens during warmup and trip the quota. Their repro script attached below.

Sasha (Backend): This matches a bug I vaguely remember: when a KV cache miss occurs, the runtime can fall back to re-streaming the full prefix as new tokens, but we may be charging both the cached copy and the regenerated tokens in the accounting window if the batching pipeline duplicates requests across workers. That would explain both higher counted tokens and the negative X-Quota-Remaining if the quota update race ran twice.

Priya (SRE): Can someone paste a minimal repro we can run in staging? Jordan, you mentioned they provided one?

Jordan (Support): Yes. Repro (customer reported):

1) Wait 10+ minutes idle to ensure KV TTL evicts (they set small TTL for test).
2) Send 10 parallel requests with a long prompt (prefill cached key). All succeed.
3) Immediately send 200 small follow-up requests (short messages, same key). Roughly 40% return 429.

Customer provided a curl script — simplified here: 

```
# warmup
for i in {1..10}; do \
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "X-Client-Id: acme-123" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-medium","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<long-prefill>"}]}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions &
done; wait

# burst
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "X-Client-Id: acme-123" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-medium","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions &
done; wait
```

They also captured response headers showing a bunch of `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` but some responses include `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 85` — inconsistent.

Priya (SRE): Thanks — I'm going to run this against staging with the client's client-id to try to reproduce. Quick checklist: which billing account/quota bucket? Do we have a per-client token rate limiter + a global pool limiter?

Eli (Billing): Hosted customers are in per-account quota buckets (monthly and short-term burst window). We also have a global per-region burst controller. The accounting path uses a central counter with optimistic updates that can be rolled back if a worker fails. If two workers both charge for the same logical request due to batching duplication, counters can overshoot. Negative remaining suggests we subtracted too much and then the periodic reconciler reported the corrected value later.

Sasha (Backend): I'm going to instrument the rate-limiter to log the allocation decisions for that client-id on staging. If it's the duplication case, we'll see two allocations with the same request hash within <1s. Also will check KV cache hit/miss logs — specifically the sequence where warmup hits go to one shard and the burst goes to others.

rate-limiter-bot: ALERT: Quota anomaly detected for client acme-123 — short-term burst exceedance events: 42 in last 5m. (auto-posted)

Jordan (Support): Customer also reports that when they add a tiny sleep (100ms) between requests the 429s drop dramatically. So it feels like a burst window exhaustion rather than strict per-request throttling. They want us to "fix" or advise a mitigation.

Priya (SRE): Dev notes from my quick investigation on staging: I reproduced the majority of the 429s when KV warmed on a different worker group. Observed sequence: warmup requests routed to worker A (populates KV), immediate burst routed across workers A/B/C. Some of the small requests hit a path that treats the prefix regeneration as chargeable tokens because the KV was considered expired locally — worker B asked for a full generation then we double-charged. I saw the duplicated token accounting with request hashes like `req-hash-9f3a`.

Sasha (Backend): Proposed immediate mitigation (hotfix): 1) ensure KV cache hits are deterministically authoritative (single source of truth) during the warmup window; 2) throttle per-client burst limiter to prefer returning 202 or queueing instead of double-charging; 3) add idempotency check for token accounting when a request hash is seen twice within 1s. I can land a small patch to short-circuit accounting duplication.

Eli (Billing): For customers: short-term workaround = increase client-side space between parallel requests (e.g., 100-200ms), enable exponential backoff on 429s, and optionally request a temporary raise on short-term burst allowance while we fix. We should also add a clear note in Support KB about KV warmup interactions.

Jordan (Support): I'll send the immediate mitigation steps to ACME: 1) advise 100ms between requests or use a small request queue, 2) enable client-side backoff on 429, 3) we'll run a hotfix and report back in 2 hrs.

Priya (SRE): Patch status: I replicated locally and wrote a unit test that fails before the fix (dup accounting). Patch will: add an in-memory dedupe per-request-hash in the accounting path and a short TTL (2s). This prevents two workers from both charging the same logical request if the hash propagation race occurs. Also toggled a flag to include `X-Quota-Remaining` consistently in the response so customers know exact remaining tokens. Rolling to staging now.

Sasha (Backend): Deployed to staging (+logs). Re-run Jordan's burst script there and confirm?

Jordan (Support): Running on staging with acme-123 now... initial warmup+burst run: before patch 45% 429s; after patch run showing 2% 429s. Logs show single allocation per req-hash. Nice.

Priya (SRE): Nice. I'll schedule a canary to prod with the dedupe and increase the per-client short-term burst window by 20% for 1 hour to absorb any user-side spikes while canary runs. If canary looks good for 30 minutes, we'll roll.

Eli (Billing): Also follow-up: we need to fix the negative `X-Quota-Remaining` values — the reconciler should never expose negative to the client. I'll file a billing ticket to clamp the header value to 0 or actual positive remaining and add a reconciliation log.

Jordan (Support): I'll update the ACME case with the workaround and ETA for prod fix; include recommended client change (100ms sleep or request queue) and invite them to test again after patch.

rate-limiter-bot: STATUS: Canary started for dedupe-patch in prod region us-east-1. 10% traffic. (auto)

Sasha (Backend): After canary completes we should also add an integration test that simulates KV warmup + concurrent burst to catch regression. I'll add to our e2e harness.

Priya (SRE): Closing loop: root cause = race between KV shard warmup and our optimistic token accounting leading to duplicate charges in the short-term burst window. Fix = dedupe accounting by request-hash + safer KV authoritative check + consistent quota headers. Workarounds = client-side spacing/backoff and temporary burst allowance.

Jordan (Support): Thanks everyone — ACME notified. Will re-open if they see anything else.

Sasha (Backend): Filing follow-ups: ENG-PR-2234 (dedupe accounting), ENG-TEST-889 (e2e), BILL-140 (clamp quota header).

Eli (Billing): I'll update billing docs and check for any other accounts that saw negative remaining values in last 48h.

Jordan (Support): Marking thread as resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
